text: A pull request title, which becomes the squash commit subject, has the form `type(scope): outcome (<task id>)` with a Conventional Commits type.
why: A squash merge turns the title into the only subject on the base branch; titles without a type and id stopped being traceable.

text: A commit that completes a managed task ends with a `Ticket: <id>` trailer; a commit that leaves the task open carries `Refs: <id>` instead.
why: Delivery stays traceable to its task, and the branch that names a ticket must close it before it merges.

text: Only the lead changes task status, through `krn task`; a worker never edits, closes or deletes a tracker file.
why: Workers running as the lead edited tracker state outside their scope in 11 of 20 units.

text: A task record states Why, Outcome and Proof; the pull request body is generated from the record instead of written by hand.
why: The pull request is the delivery record, so its problem statement and proof come from the task that defined them.

text: A change is integrated only after the repository's full required CI check passes on the exact head commit; local runs cover lint, typecheck and touched tests.
why: One required check on the exact head is the only gate; local green on another tree proves nothing about the merged one.

text: Agent notes, plans, logs and scratch files go under the git-ignored `.krn/` directory, never into tracked files or the repository root.
why: Agent state is repository-local and must stay out of the tracked project inputs.

text: A session cannot end while the tests related to its change are red, and the finish gate fails closed when it cannot run them.
why: A gate that lets a session end on an unrun or red test turns a broken tree into a delivered one.

text: Adoption proves the finish gate in the adopted repository by breaking one existing test, seeing the gate refuse, and restoring the test.
why: A gate that was never seen refusing may be wired to nothing.

text: A fixed defect gets its regression test at the lowest layer that reproduces it.
why: Low-layer tests fail fast and name the broken unit.

text: Every integration or forward is tested against its real receiver or a verbatim capture of the receiver's output, never against a hand-made imitation.
why: An integration is only proven where it is received.

text: A change does not remove assertions, add skip, only or todo markers, or delete a test whose target stays, unless its pull request states `Weakens-tests: <reason>`.
why: Weakening a test is the cheapest way to turn a red check green without fixing anything.

text: When a task names an input or output format, at least one test feeds the plainest hand-written example of that format exactly as the task words it.
why: A reader tested only on its own tool's output rejects the short, plain forms real callers send.

text: Each parallel lane works in its own git worktree and branch, so no two writers share a checkout.
why: Two writers in one checkout overwrite or commit each other's edits.

text: Never change the git stash stack with a bare `git stash` or `git stash pop`; set work aside with a commit.
why: Every worktree of a repository shares one stash stack, so a bare pop can take another lane's edits.

text: A test, typecheck or lint run is never piped into a text filter that hides its exit code.
why: A piped test run once printed `fail 0` while CI had 20 failures.

text: Never delete a branch or worktree whose tip exists on no remote while it names an open task.
why: A lead once deleted the only copy of a task's implementation this way.

text: Module dependencies follow a declared layer map that a check enforces; the core imports no replaceable adapter.
why: The core stays independent of adapters only while something refuses the forbidden import.

text: A repository keeps one instruction file for agents, AGENTS.md, and any other agent instruction file only points to it.
why: Two instruction files drift apart and agents follow whichever they read first.

text: Files, functions, tests and work are named by purpose and role, never by phase, ticket, round, date or version.
why: Phase and ticket names lose their meaning as soon as the phase or ticket ends.

text: Every error path has a stated exit code (64 usage, 65 invalid data, 70 internal, 75 temporary) and a message on stderr.
why: Callers and agents branch on exit codes; an unstated one makes a failure look like success or the wrong failure.

text: Values that may hold credentials, multiline ones included, are redacted before they are logged, persisted or forwarded.
why: A secret written to a log or a record leaks to everyone who can read it later.

text: A slice ends with a short retrospective whose every lesson becomes an executable check, a repository rule or a task.
why: A lesson kept only as prose is repeated; a check refuses the repeat.

text: The lead delivers one slice per pull request and lets it merge on the required check.
why: Small slices merged on one check keep review and rework bounded.
